newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Sierad Produce denies foreign link up.
newsitem.headline: Sierad Produce denies foreign link up.

text.p: Indonesia's poultry, agriculture and food firm PT Sierad Produce said on Wednesday it had no plans to link up with a foreign partner following market talk that it was a target for acquisition by a Malaysian company.
A company official, who asked not to be named, said the firm did not comment on market speculation.
Asked if Sierad had any plans a joint venture or enter into an alliance with a foreign firm, the official said: "No, so far there is no such plan."
Sierad Produce was actively traded at mid-afternoon on the Jakarta Stock Exchange with a volume of 7.3 million shares. The price was unchanged at 900 rupiah after earlier rising to 925 rupiah.
Brokers said the buying was linked to an announcement by Sierad that it had opened a restaurant in Shanghai and market talk of a possible link-up with a unnamed Malaysian firm.
The company said in a statement on Monday it had opened a 480-seat Hartz Chicken Buffet restaurant in Shanghai, China.
It said the expansion into China followed the successful operation of its Hartz Chicken Buffet restaurant in Jakarta.
The company official said on Wednesday the company planned to have another seven Hartz restaurants operating in Indonesia by the end of this year.
She said it also planned to operate 10 Hartz restaurant in Shanghai by the end of 1997.
"The remaining nine will be opened this year with an average seating capacity of 250 to 300 in each restaurant," she said.
She said the company had set a target of four years for each restaurant to reach the break-even point.
It expected the food division and poultry division to contribute 50 percent each to the company's net profit in 1997, she added.
She said the company expected to book 398 billion rupiah net profit in 1996 and 770 billion rupiah in 1997.
